title: Strings: Skill Summary
intro: Mix everything from this module: indexing, slicing, string methods and f-strings.

questions.prompt: `raw` has stray spaces and odd capitals. Store it tidied in `tidy`: no outer spaces, first letter capital, the rest lowercase.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert tidy == raw.strip().capitalize(), 'tidy should be stripped, then capitalised.'

questions.hint: `capitalize()` makes the first letter upper case and the rest lower.
questions.explanation: Strip first, or the first character would be a space.

questions.hint: Work out the slice, then add the last character.

questions.prompt: `code` looks like `ab-1234-xy`. Store the 4 digits in the middle as a **number** in `number`.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert number == int(code[3:7]) and isinstance(number, int), 'number should be the 4 middle digits as an int.'
tests.message: number should be an int from the middle digits.

questions.hint: Slice out the digits, then convert with `int()`.
questions.explanation: Slicing and converting often go together when reading codes.

questions.prompt: `shout` should be the message in capitals, but it holds something strange. Fix it.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert shout == 'FIRE DRILL', 'shout should be FIRE DRILL.'

questions.hint: A method needs brackets to actually run.
questions.explanation: Without `()` you store the method itself instead of calling it.
It returns the three pieces between the separators.

questions.prompt: Show `amount` as money in `shown`: a `$`, thousands separators and exactly 2 decimals — like `$1,234.50`.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert shown == f'${amount:,.2f}', 'shown should look like $1,234.50.'

questions.hint: Combine `,` and `.2f` in one format spec.
questions.explanation: Format specs can be combined: thousands separator, then precision.

questions.prompt: Fill in the method so `count` is the number of `e`s in `text`.
questions.hint: The method has the same name as the variable.
questions.explanation: `count` returns how many times the text appears.

questions.prompt: `full_name` holds a first and last name with messy spacing and capitals. Store the capitalised initials in `initials` (like `AL`) and `display` as `Last, First` in title case (like `Lovelace, Ada`).
questions.solution:
parts = full_name.split()
initials = parts[0][0].upper() + parts[1][0].upper()
display = f"{parts[1].title()}, {parts[0].title()}"

tests.name: initials
tests.code:
p = full_name.split()
assert initials == p[0][0].upper() + p[1][0].upper(), 'initials should be the capitalised first letter of each name.'

tests.name: display
tests.code:
p = full_name.split()
assert display == f'{p[1].title()}, {p[0].title()}', 'display should be Last, First in title case.'

questions.hint: `split()` gives the two names; index each one, then use `[0]` for its first letter.
questions.explanation: `split()` with no argument also ignores the extra spaces.

questions.hint: Repeat first, then join the capital letter.

questions.prompt: Blog addresses use a **slug**: lowercase with dashes instead of spaces. Store the slug for `title` in `slug` — e.g. `my-first-blog-post`.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert slug == title.strip().lower().replace(' ', '-'), 'slug should be lowercase with - instead of spaces.'
tests.message: Lowercase and swap spaces for dashes.

questions.explanation: Small chains of methods turn messy titles into clean web addresses.
